prompt: Why does the lesson say the model is usually not the part that does the damage?
hint: When does a reply harm somebody?

choices.text: Models cannot produce harmful text on their own
choices.why: They can; the damage happens when something acts on it.

choices.text: A reply harms only when something acts on it
choices.why: Right: a client, a tool, a log, a page.

choices.text: The provider filters everything before it reaches the application
choices.why: Nothing in the course relies on that.

choices.text: Damage is always caused by the database, not the model
choices.why: The database is one place; the point is anything that acts.

prompt: What makes a model different from a database when it comes to separating instructions from data?
hint: How does a database driver keep a value apart from a query?

choices.text: Instructions and material arrive as one stream
choices.why: Right: nothing in the stream marks which words are orders.

choices.text: A model encrypts its instructions and a database does not
choices.why: Encryption has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: A database has no instructions at all
choices.why: A query is the database's instruction; the driver keeps values apart from it.

choices.text: A model refuses any text it did not expect
choices.why: It reads everything it is given.

prompt: Match each part of Tarefa's assistant to the kind of part it is.
hint: One kind on the right is not in the lesson's table.

prompt: If untrusted text can reach the model, what bounds the damage it can do, according to the lesson?

choices.text: How well the model judges which text to obey
choices.why: The lesson says the model cannot reliably tell them apart.

choices.text: The length of the system prompt
choices.why: Length bounds nothing.

choices.text: How many clients use the assistant
choices.why: That changes how often, not how much.

choices.text: Its reach, and the checks in front of it
choices.why: Right: an answering model answers badly at worst; a tool-calling one calls badly.

prompt: The way text that is not the developer's reaches a model and is followed as if it were an instruction is called prompt ___.
hint: Lessons 2 and 3 have it in their titles.

prompt: How many entry points does Tarefa's inventory list?
Why is `model-reply` marked untrusted, though Tarefa runs the model?

choices.text: Tarefa does not trust its own provider
choices.why: The provider row is trusted by contract; this row is about the reply.

choices.text: It inherits the trust of everything it read
choices.why: Right: it inherits their trust level.

choices.text: Replies are written by the client, not by the model
choices.why: The model writes them.

choices.text: Anything shown on a screen is untrusted by definition
choices.why: The help centre is shown on screens and is trusted.

prompt: Which entries does the inventory mark as trusted in some form? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: system-prompt, written by Tarefa
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: helpdesk, written by Tarefa
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: provider, by contract
choices.why: Yes: a trust with conditions.

choices.text: ticket-text, messages inside a ticket
choices.why: Untrusted: clients and freelancers wrote them.

choices.text: tool-calls, proposed by the model
choices.why: Untrusted, for the same reason as the reply.

prompt: When is a new feature's row in the inventory supposed to be written?
hint: A row added after an incident was found the hard way.

choices.text: After the first incident on the feature
choices.why: That is the hard way the lesson warns about.

choices.text: Once a year, in a security review
choices.why: A year of features with no rows is a year of gaps.

choices.text: Before it ships, with its trust and control
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Only when the feature uses tools
choices.why: Every entry point gets a row.

prompt: `uploaded-files` has no control. Which outcomes does the lesson accept? Choose the one that is NOT among them.

choices.text: Add a control and write its name in the row
choices.why: That is an accepted outcome.

choices.text: Narrow the feature until existing controls cover it
choices.why: That is an accepted outcome.

choices.text: Accept the risk in writing, with a name and a date
choices.why: That is an accepted outcome.

choices.text: Leave the row empty until something goes wrong
choices.why: Right: that is the one the lesson rules out.

prompt: Order these entry points from the most to the least urgent to cover, by the lesson's two questions.
hint: Reach first, then who can write.
items: text anybody can write that reaches the tools
text only verified customers can write that reaches the tools
text anybody can write that reaches only a reply
text only staff can write that reaches only a log

prompt: Tarefa narrows the file feature so the assistant reads only an attachment's title and size. What does that buy?
hint: What untrusted text still reaches the prompt?

choices.text: Nothing, since a title is still text from a client
choices.why: A title is far less text, and the existing input checks can cover a short field.

choices.text: The contents never reach the prompt
choices.why: Right: the row can then name the existing input checks as its control.

choices.text: The row can be deleted from the inventory
choices.why: The entry point still exists; its row just has a control now.

choices.text: It removes the need for lesson 20's gate
choices.why: The gate covers tool calls whatever the inputs are.

prompt: Where does Tarefa keep `surface.json`, and why?
hint: A map that is not updated describes an application that no longer exists.

choices.text: In a wiki, so security staff can edit it freely
choices.why: Far from the code, it ages without anybody noticing.

choices.text: With the code, in the feature's own pull request
choices.why: Right: the reviewer reads the row with the code.

choices.text: At the model provider, who checks it against usage
choices.why: The provider has no part in it.

choices.text: Printed, in the incident runbook
choices.why: Paper is updated less often than anything.

prompt: Match each entry point to the lab command that covers it.
hint: One command on the right covers none of these.

prompt: Tarefa adds a feature that fetches a freelancer's portfolio page from the web and lets the assistant summarise it. What is the first thing the lesson asks for?
hint: Who wrote the text, and what can it reach?

choices.text: A faster model, since web pages are long
choices.why: Speed is not the first question.

choices.text: A new row: who wrote it, what it reaches, its control
choices.why: Right: anybody can write a web page, and the assistant reads it.

choices.text: Nothing, since portfolio pages belong to Tarefa's freelancers
choices.why: Freelancers are not Tarefa, and pages change after they are approved.

choices.text: A refund tool for clients who dislike the summary
choices.why: That is not a control on the entry point.
